name: Question 14
problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}],\,B={[\begin{aligned}| \\ {v}_{1} \\ |\end{aligned}]\,,[\begin{aligned}| \\ {v}_{2} \\ |\end{aligned}]\,,[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c \\ d\end{aligned}]}
$$

Consider the subspace $V=\text{Col}(A)$ spanned by the columns ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}$ of the matrix $A,$ and an orthogonal basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(A),$ shown above. Given that $B$ is derived from $V$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $\frac{d}{a}?$
worked_solution:
We proceed to find an orthogonal basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(A)$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows:

**Step 1.** We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2.** We find the vector ${v}_{2}$ orthogonal to $\text{Span}{{v}_{1}}$ using the usual formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}{a}_{2} \\  & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{2}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3.** We find the vector ${v}_{3}$ orthogonal to $\text{Span}{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}}$ using the usual formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & ={a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}\,{a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{2}}\,{a}_{3} \\  & ={a}_{3}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{2}}{{v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}}{v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-\frac{2}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-\frac{10}{20}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ -\frac{3}{2} \\ -\frac{1}{2} \\ -\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
\frac{d}{a}=\frac{(-\frac{3}{2})}{(\frac{1}{2})}=-3.
$$
